verdict: consistent: all recurring signs retain their values, and two different signs represent jīm as the compiler records.
notes: A divider splits وا | لصب in the opening. The four signs after هواه are ي م ن ا (يمنا, Yemen in the accusative); تارة has four further signs. The next word begins with the same toothed yāʾ then an upright with hooked head: يجوب. The verse reads يمنا تارة يجوب وشأما, “at times he traverses Yemen and Syria.” The two signs for قد recur at the opening of 69v l.3 and the following group is ا ر ي (أرى). Initial jīm in يجوب uses the hooked upright; medial jīm in نجما uses the oblique double bar. The normalized cipher form وشاما represents the clear copy’s وشأما; there is no extra sign for seated hamza.
fit_against_record_wording: 68 signs in lines of 12,12,12,14,12,6. يمنا lacks the second yāʾ in the recorded يمينا, while يجوب includes the preceding yāʾ missing from the recorded جوب. قد | أرى is clearly divided.
